subtitle: 猿も木から落ちる · 七転び八起き · 一期一会
notes: Famous Japanese proverbs and idiomatic encouragements. Most are pre-modern wisdom literature — knowing them gets you instant cultural credit, and they pop up in news/business writing more than English proverbs do. Includes the everyday 頑張って and お互い様 closers.
source: Hand-authored for Kanjido v1 (factual common-knowledge Japanese vocabulary).

cards.reading: さる も き から おちる
cards.context: Lit. 'even monkeys fall from trees'. Used to comfort someone after a mistake — even an expert at climbing slips occasionally.

cards.reading: ななころび やおき
cards.context: The Japanese 'never give up' proverb. The math (7 falls but 8 standings) implies you started standing.

cards.reading: いし の うえ に も さんねん
meanings: 3 years on a stone (warms even stone)
cards.context: Lit. 'three years even on a stone'. Even sitting on a cold stone, you'll warm it eventually with patience.

cards.word: 塵も積もれば山となる
cards.reading: ちり も つもれば やま と なる
meanings: dust piled high becomes a mountain
cards.context: Small actions accumulate into big results. The Japanese 'compound interest' proverb.

cards.reading: でる くい は うたれる
meanings: the nail that sticks out gets hammered down
cards.context: Famous proverb about Japanese conformity culture. Standing out attracts criticism.

cards.word: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず
cards.reading: にと を おう もの は いっと を も えず
cards.context: Trying to do too many things at once → accomplish none.

cards.reading: ひゃくぶん は いっけん に しかず
meanings: seeing once is better than hearing 100 times
cards.context: Direct equivalent of 'a picture is worth a thousand words'.

meanings: if in a hurry, take the long way
cards.context: Slow and steady wins. The shortcut often costs more.

cards.reading: かえる の こ は かえる
meanings: the child of a frog is a frog

cards.reading: しらぬ が ほとけ
cards.context: The peace of mind that comes from not knowing something troubling.
Tea-ceremony origin. Every encounter is unique, never to be repeated — treat it accordingly. Often used to invoke mindfulness.

cards.word: 井の中の蛙大海を知らず
cards.reading: いのなかの かわず たいかい を しらず
meanings: a frog in a well doesn't know the ocean
cards.context: Often shortened to 井の中の蛙. About narrow worldviews.

cards.reading: ふくすい ぼん に かえらず
meanings: spilt water won't return to the tray
no use crying over spilt milk

cards.context: Not technically a proverb but the most-used Japanese phrase of encouragement. Said before exams, sports, work, anything difficult. From 頑張る = to persist.

meanings: we're both in the same boat
cards.context: Said when accepting thanks or apology — 'don't mention it, we both do this for each other'. Uniquely Japanese reciprocity concept.
